key_insight: Elastic-stress birefringent strands in an ordered microporous medium drive a non-monotonic transition from steady flow to chaos and back toward ordered flow as Weissenberg number increases.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and potentially control pressure-drop variability and flow instabilities in viscoelastic microfluidic and porous-media systems by tuning operating conditions and solid volume fraction.
method: Numerical study of viscoelastic fluid flow through staggered cylindrical micropillars in an ordered microporous medium.
Examined how elastic-stress strand formation, fluctuation, and interconnection evolve with increasing Weissenberg number.
Separated pressure drop into mean and fluctuating contributions and related both to chaotic flow behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports monotonic growth in the mean pressure-drop component but non-monotonic variation in the fluctuating component, matching the observed non-monotonic chaos and total pressure-drop trends across Weissenberg number and solid volume fraction.
watch_item: Because the conclusions depend on an idealized ordered microporous geometry and simulated flow conditions, transfer to irregular real porous media may require additional validation.
paper_title: Non-monotonic variations in pressure drop and chaos in viscoelastic fluid flows through an ordered microporous medium
